speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are presenting with a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. To help me determine the cause, how long has this lesion been present, and what does it look like in detail?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum

Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the rapid progression of the ulcer following trauma (the "ant bite"), I suspect Pyoderma Gangrenosum rather than an infection. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, ESR, CRP, and Wound Culture. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_of_lesion.

REQUEST IMAGES: Full-body dermatological scan focusing on the right leg.
